answer: When many keys spend from one parent coin, admission is cheap to fake. Open two contrast escrows at never-cosigned desks: a 14-POA jade lot and a 16-POA pearl lot, funded by keys with nine-epoch disjoint ancestry. A juniper clock ticks every 95 minutes; each desk posts a receipt with opposite height parity, plus a running xor of both receipt ids on-ledger. Fee 0.38 POA; lots unlock after 4 epochs if every tick verifies. Peers recompute ancestry, parity, and xor at checkpoint. A shared ancestor, same-parity pair, or forged xor slashes 36 percent to the reporting desk and mutes the key 6 epochs.
